governance.attested_by: miso21 cc-border-anchor 2026-06-28 (KEEPER on faithfulness grounds, supersedes miso18-seam-export-cap)
governance.note: TWO measured-grounded structural levers on top of miso18 (export cap), each correcting a structural mis-representation, neither tuned to a residual. LEVER 1 -- cc_intermediate_split (--cc-intermediate-split): MISO's combined-cycle fleet runs intermediate/baseload (measured CAMPD median CF 50-150 %, mean ~90 %; ALL 39 CC_REGULAR plants in thermal_tranches_MISO.csv clear the 50 % cut), but inherited the CC_REGULAR offer curve fit to ERCOT's duct-fire-heavy 2x1 peaker CCs (Colorado Bend II / Wolf Hollow II): a rising start-cost-amortized econ ramp (econ_low 1.06 -> econ_high 1.27) that over-prices the upper operating range of an already-committed baseload CC, whose incremental energy is near its flat full-load heat rate (~0.93x its own average), so the upper econ tranches sat above the clearing price and the model under-ran the CC fleet. fleet.cc_intermediate_plants(iso, threshold) selects the measured median-CF>=threshold cohort; fleet._offer_curve_for_group routes it to the new CC_INTERMEDIATE curve (econ 0.95 -> 1.08, the measured flat near-baseload incremental cost), KEEPING the physically-real F-class duct-burner peak (2.25) and the per-plant peaking band (cc_peaking_per_plant) -- only the operating-range ramp is corrected, never the duct-fire peak (lowering the peak would be an unphysical fit to volume, rule #11). LEVER 2 -- miso_pjm_border_anchor (--miso-pjm-border-anchor): the MISO-Central seam physically clears against PJM's WESTERN border zones (ComEd / AEP-Ohio / ATSI), but the PJM neighbor price was anchored to PJM's SYSTEM-average realized RT LMP, which is pulled up by the eastern load centres (NJ / Dominion), so the import was over-priced and MISO under-imported over its largest seam. constants.MISO_PJM_BORDER_HR_BY_YEAR re-anchors the per-year HR to the equal-weight mean of the three MISO-facing PJM generator hubs (CHICAGO GEN / AEP GEN / ATSI GEN), as HR_border[y] = HR_system[y] x (mean border-hub RT LMP / mean PJM system RT LMP); transmission.inject_reference_price_mc swaps the PJM spec's hr_by_year for this table when the flag is set. The discount deepens in the tight years (ratio 0.981 / 0.956 / 0.936 for 2023/24/25) as eastern-PJM congestion widens, so 2023 (already matched on interchange) barely moves while 2024/2025 cheapen and clear more import up to the measured deliverability cap. Both levers trace to measured inputs (CAMPD median CF; PJM zonal RT LMP) that regenerate for a forward year and respond to changed conditions; both assign an offer/price SHAPE, never pin measured output, and neither reads MISO's own interchange (rules #11/#12). RESULT vs miso18: net-interchange duration RMSE 2024 1252 -> 1051 MW, 2025 2037 -> 1717 MW; total net-interchange |error| 23.5 -> 20.5 TWh; gas |error| vs EIA-923 (3yr) 55.1 -> 50.8 TWh. The export cap (miso18) is retained byte-for-byte.
governance.validation_note: Reproducible end-to-end. LEVER 1: fleet.cc_intermediate_plants('MISO', 50.0) returns the 39-plant baseload cohort; tests/test_cc_intermediate_split.py asserts off=byte-identical (CC_REGULAR econ_high 1.27), on=routed (CC_INTERMEDIATE econ_high 1.08, duct-burner peak unchanged), non-cohort plants stay on CC_REGULAR, and a missing CC_INTERMEDIATE entry falls back to CC_REGULAR. LEVER 2: scripts/derive_miso_pjm_border_hr.py regenerates MISO_PJM_BORDER_HR_BY_YEAR = {2023: 10.99, 2024: 12.9, 2025: 11.4} from the measured PJM RT LMP extract (within rounding of the committed constant); neighbor_heat_rate on the border-swapped PJM spec returns the lower per-year HR (2024 13.49 -> 12.9). Both default OFF: every prior keeper and every other ISO is byte-identical (127 unit tests pass incl. tests/test_transmission.py, test_neighbor_price.py, test_miso_seam_flow_limit.py, test_cc_intermediate_split.py). The LP run log prints 'reference-price interface ... ; PJM seam re-anchored to its western (ComEd/AEP/ATSI) border hubs'. Solved 2023/2024/2025 in one --year invocation to results/calibration/MISO/miso21_cc_border (solo; per-year RSS released between years, no cross-year dependency); P2 commitment off (MISO default). Per-fuel vs EIA-923 (model / 923): 2023 gas 225.9/249.0 coal 164.8/184.0; 2024 gas 238.2/257.8 coal 163.0/175.1; 2025 gas 215.7/207.6 coal 215.2/201.0. Net interchange (EIA +=export, model / actual): 2023 -38.9/-37.9, 2024 -16.8/-23.1, 2025 -5.7/-19.0.
governance.git_note: Two new default-OFF flags, MISO-only: --cc-intermediate-split (ScenarioConfig.cc_intermediate_split / cc_intermediate_cf_threshold) and --miso-pjm-border-anchor (ScenarioConfig.miso_pjm_border_anchor). With both unset, build is byte-identical for every ISO and year (forecast included). The export cap (--miso-seam-export-limit, reconstructed this session after the original miso18 source commit was lost before push) and all prior MISO levers are unchanged.

model_miss_notes: The exceptions ledger is EMPTY by design: every out-of-tolerance criterion is a genuine MODEL MISS to fix in a later lever, NOT an accepted measured-input limitation, so the determination is honestly NOT-YET (a structural step beyond miso18, not a pass). The two levers move the right direction but do not close the residual, which localizes to: (1) RESIDUAL GAS-CC UNDER-RUN 2023/2024: gas 225.9 vs 249.0 and 238.2 vs 257.8 EIA-923 (-23 / -20 TWh) -- the CC duty-curve lever closed ~6-7 TWh of it, but a ~20 TWh gap remains; the CC fleet still does not fully clear at the modeled MISO LMP level, pointing to a deeper gas merit / availability / coal-competition root (the flatter curve lets CC win some mid-merit but it also cannibalizes coal -4 to -6 TWh rather than adding net thermal). (2) 2025 DEAR-GAS COAL OVER-RUN: coal 215.2 vs 201.0 EIA-923 (+14.2 TWh) -- the same dominant 2025 miss flagged at miso18 (the coal take-or-pay / PRB passthrough offer level in dear gas), unaddressed here and unmasked once the export cap removed the spurious South export. (3) IMPORT UNDER-RUN 2024/2025: net interchange -16.8 vs -23.1 and -5.7 vs -19.0 -- the border anchor improved the duration-curve RMSE and closed ~2-3 TWh, but MISO still under-imports by ~6 / ~13 TWh; the residual is a MISO-LMP-LEVEL item (MISO's own dual sits too close to the re-anchored PJM border to pull the full measured eastern transfer) rather than a closable price adder. (4) ENERGY-BALANCE metric: EB (model gen vs EIA-930 itemized net gen) reads -13.7 / -7.5 / -0.2; the 2024 figure regresses vs miso18 (-5.8) BECAUSE lever 2 correctly imports more (so domestic gen falls), and the EIA-930 MISO published Demand / Net-generation / Total-interchange do not cleanly reconcile (model load served ~645 TWh matches EIA-930 Demand 642.9 in 2024, while EIA-930 itemized net gen 636.1 implies a different import than the -23.1 interchange) -- so the EB tolerance is partly an EIA-930 MISO data-imbalance artifact, not a model demand error. None of these is closable by an adder/haircut/pin/rescale to a residual (rule #12); each is a separate measured-grounded lever (coal dear-gas offer; MISO LMP level / SPP-South seam pricing; the EIA-930 net-gen reconciliation).
